steps.title: Clean wafer and plasma‑clean
steps.instruction: Rinse the polished silicon wafer sequentially with acetone, isopropanol, and water; air‑dry; set hotplate to 200 °C; perform plasma cleaning with a 30 % O₂ / 70 % N₂ gas mix using the program: Pressure 0, Power 150 W, EndPt 100 s, Temp 25 °C, BP/RP 90, RF tuning 30 % (manual vacuum bleed, load wafer polished side up, run program, switch RF to Auto, minimize reverse power, finish, vent, remove wafer, re‑establish vacuum, turn off components).

steps.title: Prepare mask aligner
steps.instruction: Turn on mask aligner components, gas and vacuum lines; power on UV lamp and allow a 10‑min warm‑up.

steps.title: First SU‑8 layer spin coat
steps.instruction: Place wafer polished side up on hotplate for 20 min at 200 °C to dry; transfer wafer to centre of 100‑mm spin‑coater carousel, engage vacuum; spin 10 s at 500 rpm (accel 266 rpm/s), then 35 s at 1500 rpm (accel 532 rpm/s) while adding two drops cyclopentanone at 1500 rpm; dispense 6 mL SU‑8 2005 evenly, avoid side drips; wait 3 min for bubbles to rise; continue spin program; lift cover slowly; edge‑bead removal with cyclopentanone‑dampened wipe; release vacuum, remove wafer; if layer non‑uniform, clean with isopropanol and restart.

steps.title: First SU‑8 soft bake
steps.instruction: Heat wafer from room temperature to 95 °C on a hotplate (initially off); hold 95 °C for 4 min; turn off hotplate and cool on plate for 10 min.

steps.title: First UV exposure
steps.instruction: Load mask 1 (chrome side up) into mask holder for 100‑mm wafers; align wafer using alignment marks; expose to UV with parameters: Exposure 95 mJ/cm², Mode Vacuum, PreVac 15 s, FullVac 10 s, Purge 10 s, WEC Continuous.

steps.title: First development and post‑bake
steps.instruction: Place wafer photoresist side up in 1 L flask; pour developer to cover; agitate 30 s; remove wafer; rinse with fresh developer then isopropanol; dry with N₂; place wafer on cooled hotplate, heat to 95 °C and incubate 1 min.

steps.title: Second plasma clean before second layer
steps.instruction: Repeat plasma cleaning (Table 3) with Pressure 0, Power 100 W, EndPt 20 s, Temp 25 °C, BP/RP 90, RF 30 % O₂/N₂.

steps.title: Second SU‑8 layer spin coat
steps.instruction: Dry wafer 20 min at 200 °C on hotplate; centre wafer on spin‑coater; spin 14 s at 500 rpm (accel 266 rpm/s), then 37 s at 3000 rpm (accel 532 rpm/s); dispense 6 mL SU‑8 2010 evenly; wait 9 min for bubbles; continue spin; lift cover slowly; edge‑bead removal with cyclopentanone‑dampened wipe; release vacuum, remove wafer.

steps.title: Second SU‑8 soft bake
steps.instruction: Heat wafer from room temperature to 85 °C on hotplate (initially off); hold 85 °C for 15 min; turn off hotplate and cool on plate for 10 min.

steps.title: Second UV exposure
steps.instruction: Load mask 2 (chrome side up) into mask holder; align using marks from first exposure; expose with parameters: Exposure 150 mJ/cm², Mode Vacuum, PreVac 15 s, FullVac 10 s, Purge 10 s, WEC Continuous.

steps.title: Second development and post‑bake
steps.instruction: Place wafer on cooled hotplate, heat to 85 °C and incubate 10 min; remove mask; turn off mask aligner and UV lamp; place wafer photoresist side up in 1 L flask; pour developer, agitate 3 min; remove wafer; rinse with fresh developer then isopropanol; repeat rinse; dry with N₂.

steps.title: Prepare PDMS mixture
steps.instruction: Pre‑heat oven to 75 °C; weigh 30 g PDMS base and 3 g curing agent into a 50 mL conical tube; cap and mix on a lab roller for 45 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Clean nanoports
steps.instruction: Sonicate 12 nanoports in 2 % Hellmanex for 20 min; rinse three times with filtered DI water; sonicate in 70 % EtOH for 20 min; rinse with 100 % ethanol.

steps.title: Create tape barrier and pour first PDMS layer
steps.instruction: Apply standard lab tape around wafer circumference, extending ≥2 mm below edge; place wafer in a 150 mm Petri dish; centrifuge mixed PDMS at >400 × g for 90 s at room temperature; pour 13 g PDMS onto wafer to wet surface evenly; dry nanoports at 70 °C for 30 min; place wafer with PDMS in vacuum desiccator 15 min at 60–70 cm Hg, then rapidly vent; bake wafer with PDMS at 70 °C for 15 min; test tackiness with a 200 µL pipette tip (should form a small peak).

steps.title: Place nanoports on semi‑cured PDMS
steps.instruction: Using a dissection microscope, place each of the twelve nanoports over the end of each media conduit; avoid double‑placement or mis‑alignment.

steps.title: Pour second PDMS layer and cure
steps.instruction: Pour 14 g PDMS onto wafer to cover entire surface; place wafer in vacuum desiccator 15 min at 60–70 cm Hg to remove trapped air under nanoports; return to oven at 70 °C for 3 h (or until fully cured).

steps.title: Trim device and punch ports
steps.instruction: Remove multFYLM from master; trim excess PDMS with a new razor blade; use a 1 mm biopsy punch to make a through‑hole through each nanoport and its underlying conduit; remove punched PDMS core with fine tweezers; inspect and remove residual PDMS particles.

steps.title: Clean device and cover glass, plasma bond
steps.instruction: Sonicate multFYLM in 100 % isopropanol for 30 min; dry on hotplate at 70 °C for 2 h; place multFYLM and cleaned cover glass (prepared by 2 % Hellmanex 1 h agitation, rinse twice with DI water, twice with isopropanol, dry on foil at 70 °C for ≥2 h) in plasma cleaner; evacuate chamber ≥1 min; set RF high for 20 s; immediately remove; immediately place cover glass (clean side) onto multFYLM centre, apply light pressure to bond.

steps.title: Prepare microfluidic tubing
steps.instruction: Sonicate all fittings in 2 % Hellmanex 20 min, rinse three times with DI water, sonicate in 100 % ethanol 20 min, rinse with ethanol, dry on hotplate at 70 °C ≥30 min; cut twelve 60 cm tubes, square ends; bend a 95° angle 17 mm from each tube end using a Bunsen burner; for six waste tubes attach F‑333N coned nut (threads away), F‑142N ferrule (blunt end toward bend), leaving 1–2 mm tubing beyond ferrule; for six media tubes attach F‑333N coned nut, F‑142N ferrule, P‑215 flangeless nut (threads toward straight end), P‑272 ferrule (blunt end away), P‑658 Luer adapter (screwed onto flangeless nut, sandwiching ferrule); connect each media line to a waste line with P‑235 connectors; store prepared tubing in ethanol or sterile water until use.

steps.title: Prepare microscope and stage heaters
steps.instruction: Turn on microscope, camera, shutter controller, stage, objective heater (set empirically to achieve 30 °C at 60× air objective), stage heater (set empirically to achieve 30 °C at device), LED white light source; launch NIS Elements (or equivalent) software; select ‘Neo/Zyla’ image grabber if prompted; move 10× objective into position.

steps.title: Prepare media and cell cultures
steps.instruction: Make 1 L YES 225 agar (36.13 g YES 225 powder + 20 g agar, add DI water to 1 L, autoclave, pour 25 mL into sterile plates); make 1 L YES 225 liquid (36.13 g powder, DI water to 1 L, filter‑sterilize); make 1 L YES 225 liquid for experiments (same as above); prepare 1 mL sterile 20 % BSA in a conical tube; streak glycerol‑stock cells onto agar plates 4 days before experiment, incubate 30 °C until colonies form, then store at room temperature; pick a 2–3‑day colony, inoculate 10 mL YES 225 in a test tube, grow overnight at 30 °C shaking; when OD₅₉₅ = 0.1 inoculate fresh 10 mL YES 225, grow 4–6 h to OD₅₉₅ = 0.5–1.0; degas YES 225 liquid by placing bottle cap loose in vacuum desiccator for 15 min immediately before loading syringes.

steps.title: Prime syringes and fluid lines
steps.instruction: Load N (number of flowpaths to be used, typically 3–4) 10 mL syringes with 70 % ethanol; run syringe pump (B‑D Plastipak 10 mL syringe) for 5 min at 1 mL/min to flush lines; replace syringes with DI water, repeat pump run; replace with degassed YES 225 media syringes (attach large syringe needle to avoid bubbles), remove any air bubbles, run pump at 1 mL/min for 1 min (custom syringe diameter 31.75 mm) to replace water with media.

steps.title: Mount multFYLM on heated stage
steps.instruction: Retrieve multFYLM, attach to heated stage insert using spring metal clips or lab tape; orient device with entrance ports closest to user and parallel to imaging area; connect waste lines to exit ports, media lines to entrance ports (avoid lines over imaging regions); keep media lines sterile (store in open conical tubes).

steps.title: Load cells into entry ports
steps.instruction: Transfer 400 µL each cell culture into separate microfuge tubes; add 100 µL sterile 20 % BSA to each tube; vortex 1 min; using a micropipette, dispense 40 µL cell‑BSA mixture into each entry port, tip just above port base to minimise air; observe cells flow into channels under white light with 10× objective.

steps.title: Establish initial flow and connect media
steps.instruction: Set syringe pump to 40 µL/min and run; as YES media exits each media line, attach line to corresponding entry port using a drop‑to‑drop connection (no torque, avoid air bubbles, avoid cracking cover glass); watch cells fill channels starting at entry ports.

steps.title: Run loading flow program
steps.instruction: Program syringe pump: 1 min at 55 µL/min followed by 14 min at 5 µL/min; repeat this 725 times to fully load channels.

steps.title: Configure multi‑dimensional image acquisition
steps.instruction: In NIS Elements, select 60× air objective, enable Perfect Focus System (PFS); bring left‑most used flowpath into view; load ROI file FYLM_ROI_2X2_new.camroi; set ND Acquisition folder and filename (auto‑append three‑digit number); set Time interval (e.g., 2 min) and total duration ≤36 h; set Z: in‑focus plane plus 4 µm offset (step 4, 2 steps, Below –4, Above 0); set λ: select optical configurations for each fluorophore, determine exposure times experimentally, collect fluorescence only at ‘Home’ Z position; set XY: tile positions in loop pattern; verify parameters (Table 5 example); press ‘Run’.

steps.title: Monitor experiment and save data
steps.instruction: Observe first few imaging cycles to confirm focus and flow; check experiment at least once per day for errors; after 24 h press ‘Finish’ to end the day’s acquisition and save files (or use File → Save); continue daily monitoring until experiment completes.
